title: Mean, Median, Range and IQR; Statistical Questions
seo_title: Grade 6 Mean, Median, Range and IQR Worksheets (TEKS 6.12C, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.12B use the graphical representation of numeric data to describe the center, spread, and shape of the data distribution; 6.12C summarize numeric data with numerical summaries, including the mean and median (measures of center) and the range and interquartile range (IQR) (measures of spread), and use these summaries to describe the center, spread, and shape of the data distribution; 6.13B distinguish between situations that yield data with and without variability
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 statistics worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.12B, 6.12C and 6.13B: statistical questions, mean, median, mode, range, outliers and IQR, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Center: mean and median. Spread: range and IQR.
key_sub: Order the data for the median. An outlier moves the mean more than the median.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A statistical question expects answers that vary: How many hours do students sleep?
  • Center: the mean (add, then divide by how many) and the median (the middle value in order).
  • Spread: the range (max − min) and the IQR (Q3 − Q1).
  • An outlier pulls the mean toward it but changes the median very little.

Examples

Example

3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 9, 9

Mean: 49 ÷ 7 = 7

Median: 8

Range: 9 − 3 = 6

Answer: mean 7, median 8

Example

Q1 = 5, Q3 = 9

IQR = 9 − 5

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Finding the median without ordering the dataPut the values in order first.
Dividing by the wrong count for the meanDivide by how many values there are.
Calling a one-answer question statisticalStatistical questions expect many different answers.

faq.a: Summarize numeric data with numerical summaries, including the mean and median (measures of center) and the range and interquartile range (IQR) (measures of spread), and use these summaries to describe the center, spread and shape of the data distribution.

faq.q: Mean or median: which is better with an outlier?
faq.a: The median, because an outlier changes it very little.

items.q: Which is a statistical question?
c: How long does it take students in Grade 6 to get to school?
How tall is the flagpole at our school?
How old is my brother?
How much does this backpack cost?
items.e: A statistical question expects answers that vary, so you collect many data values. How long does it take students in Grade 6 to get to school?

items.q: Which is not a statistical question?
c: How many hours do students in our class sleep on school nights?
What were the high temperatures in San Antonio each day last month?
What is the capital of Texas?
How much do cars at the dealership cost?
items.e: This question has only one answer, so there is no variability in the data. What is the capital of Texas?

items.q: The prices of 5 books at a used-book sale, in dollars, are 9, 5, 3, 7, 15. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 3, 5, 7, 9, 15. With 5 values, the middle one is the 3rd: 7. (The middle of the unsorted list, 3, is not the median.)

items.q: The weights of 10 puppies at a shelter, in pounds, are 22, 10, 9, 7, 16, 19, 19, 14, 10, 19. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 19 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 19, not the count 3.

items.q: The ages of 6 cousins, in years, are 4, 16, 10, 12, 3, 4. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 16 − 3 = 13. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: The heights of 8 tomato plants, in inches, are 29, 15, 12, 17, 18, 31, 31, 34. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 12, 15, 17, 18, 29, 31, 31, 34. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 18 and 29. The median is their mean: (18 + 29) ÷ 2 = 23.5.

items.q: The numbers of students on 7 school buses are 50, 35, 31, 47, 44, 36, 34. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 31, 34, 35, 36, 44, 47, 50. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 36. (The middle of the unsorted list, 47, is not the median.)

items.q: Caleb did push-ups every day for 8 days. The numbers of push-ups he did are 23, 33, 13, 11, 13, 13, 38, 33. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 13 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 13, not the count 3.

items.q: Lucia scored these points in 7 basketball games: 7, 22, 6, 21, 16, 22, 20. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 22 − 6 = 16. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: The numbers of cars in a parking lot at 6 different times were 41, 31, 55, 57, 50, 42. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 31, 41, 42, 50, 55, 57. With 6 values, there are two middle values, the 3rd and 4th: 42 and 50. The median is their mean: (42 + 50) ÷ 2 = 46.

items.q: At swim practice, 9 swimmers counted their laps. The numbers of laps are 26, 22, 28, 24, 26, 17, 13, 16, 8. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 8, 13, 16, 17, 22, 24, 26, 26, 28. With 9 values, the middle one is the 5th: 22. (The middle of the unsorted list, 26, is not the median.)

items.q: The times, in seconds, of 10 runners in a 100-meter race are 15, 16, 22, 22, 14, 17, 18, 18, 22, 21. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 22 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 22, not the count 3.

items.q: Sofia's scores on 8 spelling tests (out of 20) are 18, 20, 15, 17, 14, 14, 12, 13. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 20 − 12 = 8. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: Grace saved money for 6 weeks. The amounts she saved, in dollars, are 5, 10, 5, 9, 21, 12. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 5, 5, 9, 10, 12, 21. With 6 values, there are two middle values, the 3rd and 4th: 9 and 10. The median is their mean: (9 + 10) ÷ 2 = 9.5.

items.q: Isaac counted the birds at a feeder on 9 mornings. The counts are 4, 11, 4, 17, 19, 13, 15, 14, 13. What is the mode?
c: 4 and 13
no mode
items.e: 4 and 13 each appear 2 times. Every other value appears once. A data set can have two modes: 4 and 13.

items.q: A teacher asked 7 students to time their walk to school. The times, in minutes, are 25, 20, 13, 22, 5, 7, 10. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 5, 7, 10, 13, 20, 22, 25. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 13. (The middle of the unsorted list, 22, is not the median.)

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, for 9 days in May were 80, 78, 65, 65, 65, 75, 69, 69, 83. What is the mode?
items.e: Count how many times each value appears: 65 appears 3 times, more than any other value. The mode is the value 65, not the count 3.

items.q: Carlos read every day for 8 days. The numbers of pages he read are 14, 26, 14, 24, 40, 42, 13, 34. What is the range?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 42 − 13 = 29. Use the greatest and least values, not the first and last in the list.

items.q: The prices of 6 books at a used-book sale, in dollars, are 10, 8, 6, 4, 6, 15. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 4, 6, 6, 8, 10, 15. With 6 values, there are two middle values, the 3rd and 4th: 6 and 8. The median is their mean: (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.

items.q: The weights of 7 puppies at a shelter, in pounds, are 7, 6, 14, 16, 17, 12, 11. What is the mode?
c: no mode
items.e: Each value appears only once, so no value is more common than the others. The data set has no mode. (The mode is never a count like 1.)

items.q: The ages of 10 cousins, in years, are 16, 16, 8, 17, 4, 6, 5, 9, 14, 6. What is the mode?
c: no mode
6 and 16
items.e: 6 and 16 each appear 2 times. Every other value appears once. A data set can have two modes: 6 and 16.

items.q: The heights of 10 tomato plants, in inches, are 32, 27, 13, 16, 33, 20, 31, 12, 13, 28. What is the median?
items.e: Sort first: 12, 13, 13, 16, 20, 27, 28, 31, 32, 33. With 10 values, there are two middle values, the 5th and 6th: 20 and 27. The median is their mean: (20 + 27) ÷ 2 = 23.5.

items.q: The ages of 7 cousins, in years, are 11, 3, 5, 15, 10, 5, 14. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 11 + 3 + 5 + 15 + 10 + 5 + 14 = 63. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 63 ÷ 7 = 9.

items.q: The heights of 5 tomato plants, in inches, are 20, 20, 32, 30, 33. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 20 + 20 + 32 + 30 + 33 = 135. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 135 ÷ 5 = 27.

items.q: At swim practice, 6 swimmers counted their laps. The numbers of laps are 8, 16, 11, 11, 8, 18. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 8 + 16 + 11 + 11 + 8 + 18 = 72. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 72 ÷ 6 = 12.

items.q: Camila scored these points in 6 basketball games: 12, 15, 8, 11, 12, 8. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 12 + 15 + 8 + 11 + 12 + 8 = 66. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 66 ÷ 6 = 11.

items.q: The weights of 5 puppies at a shelter, in pounds, are 10, 10, 13, 7, 5. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 10 + 10 + 13 + 7 + 5 = 45. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 45 ÷ 5 = 9.

items.q: The numbers of cars in a parking lot at 8 different times were 22, 29, 34, 55, 35, 59, 31, 43. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 22 + 29 + 34 + 55 + 35 + 59 + 31 + 43 = 308. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 308 ÷ 8 = 38.5.

items.q: Marcus did push-ups every day for 8 days. The numbers of push-ups he did are 39, 21, 11, 24, 31, 28, 25, 21. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 39 + 21 + 11 + 24 + 31 + 28 + 25 + 21 = 200. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 200 ÷ 8 = 25.

items.q: The times, in seconds, of 7 runners in a 100-meter race are 18, 13, 15, 19, 21, 19, 21. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 18 + 13 + 15 + 19 + 21 + 19 + 21 = 126. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 126 ÷ 7 = 18.

items.q: The prices of 5 books at a used-book sale, in dollars, are 10, 10, 4, 3, 3. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 10 + 10 + 4 + 3 + 3 = 30. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

items.q: The mean of 6 test scores is 88. What is the sum of the 6 scores?
items.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count. Sum = 88 × 6 = 528 points.

items.q: A teacher asked 6 students to time their walk to school. The times, in minutes, are 8, 7, 16, 15, 14, 24. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 8 + 7 + 16 + 15 + 14 + 24 = 84. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 84 ÷ 6 = 14.

items.q: The numbers of students on 7 school buses are 46, 46, 48, 45, 42, 37, 44. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 46 + 46 + 48 + 45 + 42 + 37 + 44 = 308. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 308 ÷ 7 = 44.

items.q: Diego saved money for 6 weeks. The amounts he saved, in dollars, are 9, 9, 5, 7, 19, 14. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 9 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 19 + 14 = 63. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 63 ÷ 6 = 10.5.

items.q: The mean weight of 6 backpacks is 11 pounds. What is the total weight of the backpacks?
items.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count. Sum = 11 × 6 = 66 pounds.

items.q: Elijah's scores on 5 spelling tests (out of 20) are 18, 12, 12, 13, 20. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 18 + 12 + 12 + 13 + 20 = 75. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 75 ÷ 5 = 15.

items.q: Noah counted the birds at a feeder on 5 mornings. The counts are 7, 19, 19, 8, 17. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 7 + 19 + 19 + 8 + 17 = 70. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 70 ÷ 5 = 14.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, for 8 days in May were 79, 82, 84, 69, 61, 69, 72, 80. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 79 + 82 + 84 + 69 + 61 + 69 + 72 + 80 = 596. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 596 ÷ 8 = 74.5.

items.q: A team scored a mean of 58 points per game in 5 games. How many points did the team score in all?
items.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count. Sum = 58 × 5 = 290 points.

items.q: Carlos read every day for 8 days. The numbers of pages he read are 40, 31, 13, 21, 32, 15, 14, 18. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 40 + 31 + 13 + 21 + 32 + 15 + 14 + 18 = 184. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 184 ÷ 8 = 23.

items.q: The ages of 6 cousins, in years, are 14, 4, 11, 4, 3, 15. What is the mean?
items.e: Add the values: 14 + 4 + 11 + 4 + 3 + 15 = 51. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 51 ÷ 6 = 8.5.

items.q: Diego rode his bike to school on 7 days. The times, in minutes, were 17, 45, 16, 16, 18, 13, 14. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 13 and 18. The value 45 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: Jayden recorded how long, in minutes, he spent on homework on 6 nights: 39, 31, 45, 40, 8, 35. The outlier, 8, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 8 there are 5 values. Their sum is 39 + 31 + 45 + 40 + 35 = 190. Mean = 190 ÷ 5 = 38. (With the outlier the mean was 198 ÷ 6 = 33.)

items.q: The numbers of visitors to a small museum on 8 days were 63, 64, 44, 52, 58, 58, 49, 172. Which measure best describes a typical value?
c: the mean, 70
the greatest value, 172
the median, 58
the range, 128
items.e: The outlier 172 pulls the mean up to 70, which is greater than every other value. The median, 58, stays in the middle of the data, so the median describes a typical value better.

items.q: The numbers of cars in a parking lot at 5 different times were 32, 36, 32, 36, 34. The mean is 34. The value 46 is added to the data. What is the new mean?
items.e: The new sum is 170 + 46 = 216, and now there are 6 values. New mean = 216 ÷ 6 = 36. (Do not just average the old mean and the new value.)

items.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 24. Five of them are 16, 22, 23, 32, 23. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 6 numbers must be 6 × 24 = 144. The known numbers add to 16 + 22 + 23 + 32 + 23 = 116. Missing number = 144 − 116 = 28.

items.q: A teacher asked 8 students to time their walk to school. The times, in minutes, are 4, 22, 6, 10, 19, 17, 21, 17. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
The numbers of pages in 7 books on a shelf are 185, 185, 243, 254, 195, 210, 212. Which number describes how much the values vary?
c: the range, 69
the mean, 212
the median, 210
the mode, 185
items.e: The mean, median and mode are measures of center: each gives one typical value. The range is a measure of variation: 254 − 185 = 69 tells how spread out the values are. So the answer is the range, 69.

items.q: The weights, in pounds, of 8 dogs at a dog park are 27, 29, 32, 33, 31, 23, 87, 19. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 19 and 33. The value 87 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: The heights, in inches, of 6 sunflowers are 72, 65, 74, 59, 70, 26. The outlier, 26, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 26 there are 5 values. Their sum is 72 + 65 + 74 + 59 + 70 = 340. Mean = 340 ÷ 5 = 68. (With the outlier the mean was 366 ÷ 6 = 61.)

items.q: The ages of 8 people at a family picnic are 34, 30, 31, 2, 30, 35, 37, 33. Which measure best describes a typical value?
c: the median, 32
the mean, 29
the least value, 2
the range, 35
items.e: The outlier 2 pulls the mean down to 29, which is less than every other value. The median, 32, stays in the middle of the data, so the median describes a typical value better.

items.q: Sofia's scores on 5 spelling tests (out of 20) are 11, 15, 16, 11, 17. The mean is 14. The value 20 is added to the data. What is the new mean?
items.e: The new sum is 70 + 20 = 90, and now there are 6 values. New mean = 90 ÷ 6 = 15. (Do not just average the old mean and the new value.)

items.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 17. Five of them are 24, 14, 23, 25, 9. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 6 numbers must be 6 × 17 = 102. The known numbers add to 24 + 14 + 23 + 25 + 9 = 95. Missing number = 102 − 95 = 7.

items.q: The heights of 9 tomato plants, in inches, are 30, 24, 22, 26, 29, 24, 34, 32, 14. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Sort first: 14, 22, 24, 24, 26, 29, 30, 32, 34. The median is 26. Leave it out of both halves. Lower half: 14, 22, 24, 24, so Q1 = 23. Upper half: 29, 30, 32, 34, so Q3 = 31. IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 31 − 23 = 8.

items.q: The prices, in dollars, of 8 T-shirts in a store are 19, 20, 14, 19, 12, 54, 14, 15. Which value is an outlier?
items.e: Most values are between 12 and 20. The value 54 is far away from all the others, so it is an outlier.

items.q: Caleb counted the emails he got on 7 days: 18, 64, 19, 14, 11, 12, 16. The outlier, 64, is removed. What is the mean of the other values?
items.e: Without 64 there are 6 values. Their sum is 18 + 19 + 14 + 11 + 12 + 16 = 90. Mean = 90 ÷ 6 = 15. (With the outlier the mean was 154 ÷ 7 = 22.)

items.q: Carlos rode his bike to school on 8 days. The times, in minutes, were 18, 17, 12, 17, 14, 18, 14, 42. Which measure best describes a typical value?
c: the range, 30
the greatest value, 42
the mean, 19
the median, 17
items.e: The outlier 42 pulls the mean up to 19, which is greater than every other value. The median, 17, stays in the middle of the data, so the median describes a typical value better.

items.q: Aaliyah counted the birds at a feeder on 5 mornings. The counts are 10, 21, 11, 13, 20. The mean is 15. The value 6 is added to the data. What is the new mean?
items.e: The new sum is 75 + 6 = 81, and now there are 6 values. New mean = 81 ÷ 6 = 13.5. (Do not just average the old mean and the new value.)

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 28. Four of them are 30, 35, 36, 20. What is the missing number?
items.e: The sum of all 5 numbers must be 5 × 28 = 140. The known numbers add to 30 + 35 + 36 + 20 = 121. Missing number = 140 − 121 = 19.

items.q: Camila recorded how long, in minutes, she spent on homework on 8 nights: 30, 26, 36, 39, 42, 41, 29, 29. Which number describes how much the values vary?
c: the mean, 34
the range, 16
the mode, 29
the median, 33
items.e: The mean, median and mode are measures of center: each gives one typical value. The range is a measure of variation: 42 − 26 = 16 tells how spread out the values are. So the answer is the range, 16.

items.q: Elijah scored these points in 7 basketball games: 22, 28, 15, 18, 19, 27, 27. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
items.e: Sort first: 15, 18, 19, 22, 27, 27, 28. The median is 22. Leave it out of both halves. Lower half: 15, 18, 19, so Q1 = 18. Upper half: 27, 27, 28, so Q3 = 27. IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 27 − 18 = 9.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, in Denver from Monday to Sunday were 50, 63, 66, 57, 48, 64, 65. What was the mean high temperature?
items.e: Add the values: 50 + 63 + 66 + 57 + 48 + 64 + 65 = 413. There are 7 values, so divide by 7: 413 ÷ 7 = 59. The mean high temperature was 59°F.

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, in Seattle from Monday to Sunday were 61, 59, 66, 61, 53, 67, 56. What was the range of the temperatures?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 67 − 53 = 14.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class grew 8 bean plants. After 3 weeks, the heights in centimeters were 22, 11, 16, 11, 15, 19, 11, 23. What was the mean height?
items.e: Add the values: 22 + 11 + 16 + 11 + 15 + 19 + 11 + 23 = 128. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 128 ÷ 8 = 16. The mean height was 16 cm.

items.q: Sofia's scores on the first 3 tests are 94, 85, 97. What score does she need on the 4th test to have a mean score of 90?
items.e: To have a mean of 90 over 4 tests, the total must be 4 × 90 = 360. So far: 94 + 85 + 97 = 276. Sofia needs 360 − 276 = 84.

items.q: Diego's scores on the first 4 tests are 90, 94, 92, 77. What score does he need on the 5th test to have a mean score of 85?
items.e: To have a mean of 85 over 5 tests, the total must be 5 × 85 = 425. So far: 90 + 94 + 92 + 77 = 353. Diego needs 425 − 353 = 72.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class grew 8 bean plants. After 3 weeks, the heights in centimeters were 16, 23, 14, 23, 14, 22, 17, 18. What was the median height?
items.e: Sort first: 14, 14, 16, 17, 18, 22, 23, 23. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 17 and 18. The median is their mean: (17 + 18) ÷ 2 = 17.5.

items.q: In a class, 6 girls read a mean of 5 books over the summer and 3 boys read a mean of 11 books. What is the mean number of books for all 9 students?
items.e: Find each total first: 6 × 5 = 30 and 3 × 11 = 33. All together: 30 + 33 = 63 books for 9 students. Mean = 63 ÷ 9 = 7. (Averaging 5 and 11 does not work, because the groups are different sizes.)

items.q: Camila averaged 18 points per game in 5 games. Then she scored 30 points in the next game. What is her new average for all 6 games?
items.e: Points before: 18 × 5 = 90. New total: 90 + 30 = 120. New average = 120 ÷ 6 = 20 points.

items.q: Valeria read for 20, 40, 45, 30, 60, 50, 55, 20, 45, 15 minutes on 10 days. What is the median number of minutes she read?
items.e: Sort first: 15, 20, 20, 30, 40, 45, 45, 50, 55, 60. With 10 values, there are two middle values, the 5th and 6th: 40 and 45. The median is their mean: (40 + 45) ÷ 2 = 42.5.

items.q: Liam saved 17, 7, 6, 10, 6, 20 dollars in 6 weeks. What is the mean amount he saved per week, in dollars?
items.e: Add the values: 17 + 7 + 6 + 10 + 6 + 20 = 66. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 66 ÷ 6 = 11.

items.q: On the red team, 4 players scored a mean of 11 points. On the blue team, 8 players scored a mean of 5 points. What is the mean score of all 12 players?
items.e: Find each total first: 4 × 11 = 44 and 8 × 5 = 40. All together: 44 + 40 = 84 points for 12 players. Mean = 84 ÷ 12 = 7. (Averaging 11 and 5 does not work, because the groups are different sizes.)

items.q: The high temperatures, in °F, in Phoenix from Monday to Sunday were 95, 98, 97, 84, 93, 89, 96. What was the median high temperature?
items.e: Sort first: 84, 89, 93, 95, 96, 97, 98. With 7 values, the middle one is the 4th: 95.

items.q: Isaac's scores in 4 bowling games are 99, 111, 139, 134. What score does he need in the next game to average 120 for all 5 games?
items.e: To have a mean of 120 over 5 bowling games, the total must be 5 × 120 = 600. So far: 99 + 111 + 139 + 134 = 483. Isaac needs 600 − 483 = 117.

items.q: Carlos scored 13, 16, 17, 14, 15 points in 5 basketball games. How many points does he need in the next game to average 18 points per game?
items.e: To have a mean of 18 over 6 basketball games, the total must be 6 × 18 = 108. So far: 13 + 16 + 17 + 14 + 15 = 75. Carlos needs 108 − 75 = 33.

items.q: On 5 quizzes, Marcus scored 10, 10, 8, 7, 10 and Gabriel scored 6, 6, 9, 8, 6. How many points greater is Marcus's mean score than Gabriel's?
Caleb averaged 22 points per game in 6 games. How many points did he score in all?
items.e: Total = mean × number of games = 22 × 6 = 132 points.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class grew 8 bean plants. After 3 weeks, the heights in centimeters were 9, 19, 19, 18, 9, 14, 22, 10. What is the difference between the mean and the median?
items.e: Mean: 9 + 19 + 19 + 18 + 9 + 14 + 22 + 10 = 120, and 120 ÷ 8 = 15. Median: Sort first: 9, 9, 10, 14, 18, 19, 19, 22. With 8 values, there are two middle values, the 4th and 5th: 14 and 18. The median is their mean: (14 + 18) ÷ 2 = 16. Difference: 16 − 15 = 1.

items.q: A basketball team scored 47, 55, 46, 59, 38, 39, 46, 42 points in its first 8 games. What was the mean number of points per game?
items.e: Add the values: 47 + 55 + 46 + 59 + 38 + 39 + 46 + 42 = 372. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 372 ÷ 8 = 46.5.

items.q: In 5 long jumps, Nevaeh jumped 10, 8, 12, 13, 12 feet and Elijah jumped 12, 8, 12, 9, 9 feet. How many feet greater is Nevaeh's mean jump than Elijah's?
A bakery sold 34, 30, 27, 50, 34, 37 muffins on 6 days. What is the range of the number of muffins sold?
items.e: Range = greatest − least = 50 − 27 = 23.
